answer: Every new identity enters through one narrow inlet: a sequential delay puzzle whose steps chain on each other, so extra cores or machines cannot shorten it. One puzzle costs about six hours of CPU before the identity can trade, grade, or vote, and each extra identity needs another full puzzle. An attacker minting 1,000 fakes faces 6,000 CPU-hours before any of them earns one saffron token of reputation, while a sparrow-sized honest newcomer pays once and keeps its standing for good. Verification is public and cheap, so shortcuts get rejected without re-running the work.
